text.p: Anglo-U.S. drugs group SmithKline Beecham Plc on Tuesday hailed its underlying growth in sales and profits as "excellent," despite difficulties with sterling and at its smallest division.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, finance director Hugh Collum said "the underlying growth is excellent, principally through new products, and we are getting good growth both in pharmaceuticals and consumer healthcare."

Collum said gross profit margins during the quarter were 4.1 percent higher across all businesses. This was helped by a 3.7 percentage point gain in pharmaceuticals, partly through an improved sales mix and also through a change in the way that U.S. pharmacy benefit manager DPS charged for its business.

Collum said DPS had switched to charging customers on a pay-per-use basis rather than through an annual capitation fee. Although this pushed revenues down 64 percent to 41 million stg in the quarter, profit margins at the division improved by 2.7 percent, he said.
